# a12s

> a12s runs AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) as durable, isolated "agent computers" in Docker. A project
> declares them in fleet.yaml or creates them from code, `a12s up` runs the Fleet, and apps send them work
> (Messages) and follow their Turns and events through the TypeScript SDK (`@coltonkirsten/a12s` on npm), the Python
> SDK (`a12s` on PyPI), a browser gateway, or an HTTP API.

This file is for coding agents building ON a12s, and it is meant to be enough on its own: every command, field,
method and file layout below is exact, so copy them rather than guessing. Current release: v0.8.1 (CLI, images,
svckit, npm and PyPI packages all share the version). You never edit or vendor a12s itself: a project changes only
its own fleet.yaml, images, Services and app code.

## Words

- Fleet: what one project runs. fleet.yaml declares it (metadata.name is the Fleet's name); the SDK and the HTTP API
  change it while it runs. Its version goes up by one with every change.
- agent computer (`AgentComputer` in code): one agent (harness + home drive + session + inbox); survives sleep and
  restarts.
- Message: work in an agent computer's inbox. `send` puts one there, even while it is busy or asleep; it is
  delivered at its next idle moment, batched with anything else pending. `send(...).wait()` (CLI: `--wait`) returns
  the Turn that delivered it. Two Messages sent back to back to an idle agent computer usually run as two Turns (the
  first starts at once), so count results across Turns, never expect them in one.
- Turn: one run of the agent that delivers every pending Message; ends completed | failed | interrupted. When
  background work ends, the agent gets a Turn by itself: turn.started {reason: "background"}, no Messages (Codex:
  computerd starts it, its prompt carries each <background-result>).
- Session: the agent's conversation. Turns continue it; a Message with fresh=true starts a new one. The harness
  process lives across Turns, so background work (a sub-agent or Bash run with run_in_background; a Codex sub-agent
  or command still running at the Turn's end) outlives its Turn.
  status shows it as background {tasks}; the agent computer stays Ready (Messages run at once) but never idle.
- Event: journal entry, {v, agentComputer, session, turn, seq, ts, type, data}. The types an app uses:
  turn.started {inbox: {messages: [{id, sender, via, …}]}, …}, text.delta {text}, tool.started {id, name, input},
  tool.finished {id, name, isError, output}, turn.finished {status, usage (the harness's own), tokens?: {input
  (without cached), output, cacheRead, cacheWrite}, error?}, egress.denied {host, port, reason}, task.started and
  task.finished {id, kind, description, status? (completed | failed | stopped | killed)}; fleet-wide only:
  agent_computer.phase {phase, error?, waiting?}; SDK-made: gap (events lost; resync). Others: docs/api.md.
- via: who really sent a Message: local (owner CLI/SDK), token:<name>, service:<name>, computer:<name>. sender is
  only the sender's own label. Trust via, not sender.
- grants.send: agent computers this agent computer (or Service) may send to. On an agent computer it adds the MCP
  tool `mcp__a12s__send` (args: computer, body; optional fresh boolean, expires seconds, replaceKey string) that
  returns a receipt, never an answer. Grants are one-way: for a reply, the other side needs its own grant back.
- Service: a non-agent container in the same Fleet (a clock, a database, an MCP server). No harness, no inbox.
- phase (exact strings, capitalized): Provisioning, Starting, Ready, Busy, Stopping, Asleep, Error; a Service can also
  be Unhealthy. `status.phase` in the SDKs, `.phase` of each `a12s status --json` entry, agent_computer.phase events.
  One waiting for a credential with no value yet stays Provisioning with `waiting: {credentials, fix}`.

## Setup (once per machine)

Needs Docker running (Docker Desktop on macOS; Docker Engine 28+ on Linux) and, for the token, the Claude Code CLI
(`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`).

```sh
brew install coltonkirsten/tap/a12s   # macOS/Linux; `a12s version` prints the release
claude setup-token                    # browser sign-in, prints a long-lived sk-ant-oat01-… token
```

Credential for `anthropic`: a `claude setup-token` token (recommended; Claude subscription) or an Anthropic API key
(`sk-ant-api…`), not a copy of your interactive Claude login. Codex: `openai` = the auth.json
form of an OpenAI API key, `{"auth_mode":"apikey","OPENAI_API_KEY":"sk-…"}` (Codex ignores a bare key).
- `a12s creds set <name>` reads ONE line when typed or pasted (not echoed), or all of stdin when piped. The setup
  token prints wrapped over several terminal lines: pasting it stores only the first piece and Turns fail to
  authenticate. Join it first: `pbpaste | tr -d ' \n' | a12s creds set anthropic`, or
  `printf %s "$TOKEN" | a12s creds set anthropic`. `creds set anthropic` refuses a value that isn't one unbroken
  sk-ant-oat01-… or sk-ant-api03-… string of about 108 characters and prints the fix; `--no-check` skips it.
- Run it in the Fleet's directory: it sets the value on the Fleet's Controller (starting it if none runs), and agent
  computers using it get it at once. From code: `fleet.credentials.set(name, value)`. Before or after `a12s up`
  both work: what names a credential with no value yet is created with a warning and waits in Provisioning
  (`waiting` in its status), then starts once it is set.
- The Controller keeps values in its state volume (credentials.json, 0600) across restarts of Docker or the
  Controller; `a12s down` removes them. No API call returns a value. A bad or expired credential fails the Turn
  (turn.finished status failed, error "Failed to authenticate: …"): set it again.

## New project

```sh
a12s init myproj && cd myproj         # fleet.yaml (defaults + one agent computer "assistant"), README, this llms.txt, AGENTS.md
a12s creds set anthropic              # see Setup for pasting the token
a12s up                               # creates the agent computers, returns when they are Ready
a12s send assistant "Reply with the single word pong." --wait
```

`a12s init` is optional (a hand-written fleet.yaml works); after `a12s init dir`, cd into dir before `creds set`.
It puts harness, image and credentials in `defaults:`, so an agent computer created from code needs only a name and
instructions, and writes `harness: { kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280 }` with no model key (the harness's
default model): add `model: haiku` yourself. Commit fleet.yaml; credential values live only in the Controller.

## fleet.yaml

```yaml
apiVersion: a12s.ai/v1alpha1
kind: Fleet
metadata: { name: team }              # DNS label; also names ~/.a12s/team/
defaults:                             # applies to every agent computer (not Services); maps merge, lists replace (credentials add)
  harness: { kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280, model: haiku }   # model: haiku | sonnet | opus | a full model id
  image: slim                         # slim | your image built FROM ghcr.io/coltonkirsten/a12s/slim:0.8.1
  credentials: [anthropic]            # names; values are set with a12s creds set (never in the file)
  egress: { allow: [] }               # deny by default; the model API needs no entry (see below)
agent_computers:
  lead:
    instructions: |                   # its CLAUDE.md (claude-code) or AGENTS.md (codex)
      You are lead. …
    grants: { send: [worker1] }
  worker1:
    files: { .claude/skills/review/SKILL.md: "…" }   # more files for its home: .claude/skills, .mcp.json
    grants: { send: [lead] }
```

Agent computer fields (all optional except a harness, image and credential, which usually come from defaults):

- harness: {kind: claude-code, version: 2.1.280, model} or {kind: codex, version: 0.154.0} with credentials
  [openai]. Use these versions (published bundles); a version that has no bundle fails `a12s up`.
- image: `slim` or a custom image ref (see Custom images).
- instructions: text written to its home as CLAUDE.md (claude-code) or AGENTS.md (codex): its standing role.
- files: {path: text}: more text files for its home, by path relative to /home/agent (`.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`,
  `.mcp.json`, `bin/tool`). A file that starts with `#!` is executable. Instructions plus files: at most 1 MiB.
  No instructions or files is fine: `hello: {}` with defaults works.
- credentials: [names]. anthropic → Claude Code, openai → Codex, github → GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, any other name →
  file /run/a12s/secrets/<name> (the agent can read that file, but not list the directory: put the exact path in its
  instructions). The list ADDS to the defaults' list (the one list that doesn't replace): with defaults [anthropic],
  `credentials: [stripe]` gives it both. A credential with no value yet doesn't fail the write: it warns and the
  agent computer waits until it is set.
- egress: {allow: [hosts]}. HTTPS to those hosts only; plain http and private addresses are refused. The harness's
  own API and sign-in hosts are always added, so `allow: []` still lets Claude Code work. Allow everything public:
  `allow: ["*"]` (quote it: a bare * is YAML alias syntax and fails to parse).
- grants: {send: [agent computers]}. uses: [services] (reach a Service's ports; an MCP port becomes a tool).
  resources: {cpu: 2, memory: 4Gi}. A Message body is at most 64 KiB.
- power: {sleepAfterIdle: 15m, wakeOnMessage: {from: [local, service:clock, computer:lead, token:web],
  maxWakesPerHour: 6}}. sleepAfterIdle is off or 1s to 7d (e.g. 5s, 15m, 2h, 1d); maxWakesPerHour 1-60. Default:
  never sleeps. Asleep (by sleepAfterIdle or a plain `sleep`), only a Message whose via is listed wakes it (no
  wildcard); `sleep --hold` keeps it asleep until `wake`, whatever is sent (status: "auto-wake suppressed").
- security: {seccomp: ./profiles/x.json}: a Docker-format seccomp profile, relative to fleet.yaml, replacing
  Docker's default for that agent computer only; `a12s up` reads the file and sends the profile itself. From the SDK
  or the HTTP API, `seccomp` is the profile's JSON object. Set it only when the image's software needs blocked
  syscalls (Chromium's sandbox: see Custom images). Only the owner sets it, not a prefix token.
- attach: {name: {host, readOnly, keep}}: a folder on this machine mounted at /home/agent/<name> (name: a DNS label,
  not bin; at most 8), so the agent works on your project in place. host: in fleet.yaml relative to it, ~/… or
  absolute (`a12s up` sends the absolute path; from the SDK or HTTP API it must be absolute). readOnly: true mounts it
  read-only. keep: [node_modules, .venv]: paths under it that live on a12s drives instead of in your folder (needs
  readOnly false). Not ~, ~/.a12s or ~/.docker. Only the owner sets it (not a prefix token, not the gateway), never
  in defaults, and only the owner changes the image of an agent computer with one. See gotchas.

Top level also takes `services:` (see Services). Change anything and run `a12s up`: it applies at each agent
computer's next idle moment, never mid-Turn, and keeps the session; changed files are written again, other files in
its home stay. The Controller pins the image a tag names when first used: to pick up a rebuilt image, use a new tag.

The live Fleet is the source of truth; fleet.yaml is optional. `a12s up` is a plain apply: the live Fleet becomes the
file, so it removes agent computers created from code and replaces changes made through the SDK or API.
`a12s export` writes the live Fleet back to fleet.yaml (instructions and files inline, seccomp profiles to
profiles/<name>.json, attach hosts relative to fleet.yaml when nearby; comments are lost): run it before `a12s up` to keep what code changed (`git diff` shows it).
Give each agent computer one owner: the file or your code.

## What the agent sees

- Its instructions (CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md for codex) are its standing role. Put the role and protocol there, not
  in Message bodies: the agent treats bodies as untrusted data from the sender.
- Each Turn's prompt lists the delivered Messages, oldest first, each as
  `<msg-… n="1" id="m_…" from="<sender>" via="<via>" at="…">body</msg-…>`, so instructions can say "when a message
  via computer:coder arrives, …".
- With grants.send it has the tool `mcp__a12s__send`. It never waits for an answer: a reply arrives later as a new
  Message (via computer:<name>) in a new Turn. The session continues between Turns, so it remembers what it sent.
- Home is /home/agent (the home drive, kept across sleep and restarts). The root filesystem is read-only; the
  agent can install into its home (`pip install --user`, `npm install`, ~/bin) if egress allows the registry.

## CLI

```sh
a12s up                               # apply fleet.yaml to the live Fleet (start the Controller if needed)
a12s export                           # write the live Fleet back to fleet.yaml and profiles/
a12s status                           # phase, inbox, power, warnings (--json for machines)
a12s send <c> "…" [--fresh] [--expires 60s] [--replace key] [--meta k=v]   # enqueue and exit; busy or asleep
a12s send <c> "…" --wait              # and stream the Turn that delivers it; exit 0 if it completed, 1 if not
a12s logs <c> [--follow]              # its journal, one "<seq> <type> <data JSON>" line per event, then exits;
                                      #   --follow keeps following (Ctrl-C). Types as in Words: turn.finished, …
a12s gateway --web dir | --dev url | -- npm run dev [--port 7012] [--allow status,events,send,inbox] [--agent-computers c1,c2] [--no-open]
a12s ui [--port 7013] [--no-open]     # the web console (npx github:coltonkirsten/a12s-console; Node.js 20+); args go to the console
a12s inbox <c> [--bodies]             # pending Messages (human table; --json for machines)
a12s inbox hold <c> | inbox resume <c> | inbox rm <c> <id>   # hold delivery (Messages still queue), release, withdraw
a12s stop <c> | sleep <c> [--hold] | wake <c>   # end the Turn and background work; sleep (--hold: only wake wakes it); wake
a12s shell <c|svc> [-- cmd…]          # audited terminal inside an agent computer or Service
a12s service ls | status <svc> | logs <svc> [-f]
a12s token create <name> --prefix biz- # <name> is a DNS label (bizapp), not the prefix. Owner powers on biz-* names
                                      #   (not seccomp or attach), nothing outside. Prints the secret (a12st_…) once, alone on
                                      #   stdout: TOKEN=$(a12s token create bizapp --prefix biz-)
a12s token create <name> --actions send,events,status,inbox,power,stop --agent-computers c1,c2|'*'   # narrow
a12s creds set <name>                 # see Setup
a12s doctor                           # every check, with its fix
a12s down                             # stop all, keep disks;  down --purge deletes them (asks)
```

Every command finds the Fleet from -F path/fleet.yaml, $A12S_FLEET, or the nearest fleet.yaml upward. `<c>` is an
agent computer's name. Every command takes `--json` (before or after it) for scripts: `a12s status --json` is
{fleet, agentComputers: [{name, phase, inbox: {pending, held, …}, …}], …} (phase directly on each entry; held is
true/false, pending a number); `a12s --json send desk "hi" | jq -r .id` gives a Message id (m_ plus 26 capitals/digits);
`a12s inbox desk --json` is the inbox object below; `a12s --json token create … | jq -r .secret`.

## SDKs (TypeScript and Python)

TypeScript: `npm install @coltonkirsten/a12s` (Node 20+, ESM; in a browser through a bundler and the gateway).
Python: `pip install a12s` (Python 3.10+; `import a12s`). Both have the same objects and methods, listed here in
TypeScript; `Py:` notes the Python form where it differs beyond the naming rules below.

```ts
import { Fleet, A12sError, NotFound } from "@coltonkirsten/a12s";
const fleet = await Fleet.connect();  // nearest fleet.yaml's Fleet, else the only running one, as owner (no token);
  // or ({ fleet }), ({ url, token }), env A12S_URL + A12S_TOKEN; in a page served by the gateway: no arguments.
  // ({ token }) alone: this machine's Fleet under another token (a prefix token's secret). Py: a12s.Fleet(fleet=…)

// create takes any agent computer field (as in fleet.yaml); the rest comes from defaults. Resolves once it is up.
const coder = await fleet.agentComputers.create("coder", { instructions: "You write and run Python.",
  egress: { allow: ["pypi.org", "files.pythonhosted.org"] } });  // Py: create("coder", instructions=…, egress={…})
  // a taken name: A12sError code "exists"; { replace: true } (Py replace=True) overwrites it
const lead = await fleet.agentComputers.get("lead");   // throws NotFound if there is none; also list()
lead.name; lead.spec; lead.effective; lead.status.phase  // as written, defaults merged, status: a snapshot
await lead.reload();                                     // refreshes it

const m = await lead.send("…", { fresh: true });    // returns at once; options sender, metadata, fresh, expires
m.id; m.state;                                      //   (seconds), replaceKey. Py: send("…", fresh=True)
const r = await lead.send("Explain TCP.").wait({    // the Turn that delivers it, once it ends; m.wait() works too,
  onEvent: (ev) => { if (ev.type === "text.delta") process.stdout.write(ev.data.text); },  // even after it ended
});                                   // also { signal }. Py: wait(on_event=lambda ev: print(ev.data["text"]))
r.status; r.text; r.id; r.error; r.messages; r.tools; r.message.id   // a Turn plus the Message it delivered

const turns = fleet.turns(["lead", "worker1"]);     // Turns as they end; no argument = every agent computer
await turns.ready();                                // connected: nothing after this is missed
for await (const t of turns) { t.agentComputer; t.text; t.status; t.tokens?.output; t.messages[0]?.via; break; }
// Py: with fleet.turns(["lead", "worker1"]) as turns:   # entering waits until connected
//         lead.send("task"); then: for t in turns: t.agent_computer, t.text …
const evs = lead.events();                          // live from now; fleet.events(names?) for several or all
await evs.ready();
for await (const ev of evs) { if (ev.type === "text.delta") ev.data.text; }   // typed by ev.type
lead.events({ turn: r.id });                        // replay one Turn from its start; ends after its turn.finished
const past = await lead.turns({ limit: 20 });       // its last finished Turns (an array), newest first

await lead.update({ instructions: "…", power: null }); // merge patch, null (Py None) = default; at its next idle
const box = await lead.inbox({ bodies: true });     // {held, holdReason?, pending, claimed, messages:
                                                    //   [{id, seq, state, sender, via, body?, replaceKey?, …}], …}
await lead.message(m.id); await lead.withdraw(m.id); // withdraw: a pending Message is removed, never delivered
await lead.hold({ reason: "triage" }); await lead.resume();   // hold delivery (sends still queue); release it
await lead.stop(); await lead.wake();               // stop the active Turn and background work; wake a sleeping one
await lead.sleep();                                 // a sender listed in wakeOnMessage wakes it
await lead.sleep({ hold: true });                   // until wake(): NO Message wakes it. Py: sleep(hold=True)
await coder.remove();                               // stops and removes it; its home drive and inbox are kept
await fleet.status();                               // every agent computer and Service: phase, inbox, power

const clock = await fleet.services.get("clock");    // fleet.services: create, get, list
await clock.sleep(); await clock.wake();            // Service: reload, update, sleep, wake, remove
const app = await fleet.tokens.create("bizapp", { prefix: "biz-" });  // owner only; app.secret shown once
const tok = await fleet.tokens.create("web", { actions: ["send", "status"], agentComputers: ["lead"] });  // also list(), remove(name)
const { version, spec } = await fleet.get();        // the whole Fleet as written. Py: .version, .spec (a dict)
await fleet.credentials.set("stripe", key);         // agent computers using it get it at once; never read back
await fleet.credentials.list();                     // [{name, set, usedBy}]; remove(name): 409 in_use while used
await fleet.replace((f) => { f.defaults!.power = { sleepAfterIdle: "15m" }; });  // If-Match, retried on conflict
// Py: fleet.replace(lambda f: f.defaults.update(power={"sleepAfterIdle": "15m"}))
```

- Python: methods, keyword arguments and attributes are snake_case (`agent_computers`, `t.agent_computer`,
  `replace_key=`, `on_event=`, `used_by`, `is_error`); options are keyword-only. Results are objects read by
  attribute, not dicts (`r.text`, `box.messages[0].via`, `t.tools[0].is_error`). Free-form JSON stays a dict with
  the API's camelCase keys: `ev.data`, a tool's `input`/`output`, `usage`, `spec`, `effective`, and nested spec
  values (`power={"sleepAfterIdle": "30m"}`). `lead.turns()` without a limit is a live stream. Close with
  `fleet.close()` or `with a12s.Fleet() as fleet:`.
- Python async: `a12s.AsyncFleet()`, the same objects with `await`, `async for`, `async with`
  (`r = await lead.send("…").wait()`, or `m = await lead.send("…")` then `await m.wait()`). Close it with
  `await fleet.aclose()` (AsyncFleet has no close()) or `async with a12s.AsyncFleet() as fleet:`.
- Errors: `A12sError` {status, code, message, fix} and `NotFound` (a 404, its subclass); streams raise
  `A12sStreamError`, and `A12sGapError` with `onGap: "throw"` (Py `on_gap="throw"`), else a gap is a `gap` event. A
  failed Turn is not an error: wait() returns it, status "failed". A write's warnings (a grant to a missing agent
  computer, a credential with no value) go to console.warn (Py `warnings.warn(a12s.A12sWarning)`).
- events() and turns() start live, and all of one Fleet's share one connection (GET /v1/events). End a stream with
  `break` or `.close()` (TypeScript also `{ signal }`). Iteration has no timeout: in Python, bound it with a thread
  or AsyncFleet and asyncio.wait_for.
- Turn: {agentComputer, id, session, status, text (all the agent said in the Turn), error?, messages: [{id, sender,
  via}], tools: [{id, name, input, output, isError}], usage, tokens?, startedAt?, finishedAt}. In TypeScript tool
  input/output and usage are `unknown`: cast them. Spec types: `AgentComputerSpec`, `FleetSpec`.

## Recipe: hand work from one agent to another

A lead dispatches to a worker with `grants.send` and gets the result back as a later Message; the app watches both.
fleet.yaml, TypeScript and Python: https://github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s-cookbook/tree/main/examples/hand-off
A worker's result is in its send call (`t.tools`, name `mcp__a12s__send`, input `{computer, body}`), not in t.text.
The receiver's Turn can finish before the sender's (a send happens mid-Turn): match Turns by agent computer and
content, never by arrival order.

## Custom images

Add tools (a toolchain, a CLI, a browser) by building FROM the slim image of your a12s release. slim is
node:24-bookworm-slim (Debian, apt) plus git, ripgrep, python3, curl, ca-certificates and computerd.

```dockerfile
# images/agent/Dockerfile; build: docker build -t my-agent:1 images/agent; use: worker: { image: my-agent:1 }
FROM ghcr.io/coltonkirsten/a12s/slim:0.8.1
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends jq ffmpeg && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

- A local tag works; a12s up pulls only images it doesn't have. The base tag is the release without the v
  (slim:0.8.1). Admission needs the `ai.a12s.computerd.version` label FROM slim sets (same minor as the CLI) and
  computerd at /opt/a12s/computerd/dist/main.js; don't remove either.
- The Dockerfile runs as root; don't set USER, ENTRYPOINT or CMD (a12s ignores them: computerd starts as root and
  runs the agent as uid 1000 with /home mounted over). Install system-wide (/usr, /opt), not into /home/agent.
- To change the image, build a new tag and change it in fleet.yaml; a pinned tag keeps its old digest.
- A browser: install Chromium (and Playwright) in the image and give that agent computer
  `security: { seccomp: ./profiles/chromium.json }` (Docker's default profile plus clone/unshare with
  CLONE_NEWUSER, setns, chroot). Never use --no-sandbox. Full Dockerfile and profile:
  https://github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s-cookbook/tree/main/examples/browser-agent

## Services

A Service is an image a12s runs next to the agent computers. It may only do what its grants say: `grants.send` lets
it enqueue Messages (they arrive via service:<name>), `uses` lets agent computers reach its ports.

```yaml
services:                             # top level, next to agent_computers:
  clock:
    image: my-clock:1                 # an image you built; it must contain /a12s/service.json
    grants: { send: [worker] }
    config: { to: worker, every: 2m, env: { TZ: UTC } }   # /run/a12s/config/config.json; its env map becomes
                                                          #   environment variables (there is no top-level env:)
    # also: credentials: [name], egress: {allow: [...]}, uses: [svc], resources, manifest (inline service.json)
agent_computers:
  worker:
    power: { sleepAfterIdle: 30m, wakeOnMessage: { from: [service:clock] } }   # only if it may sleep
```

- service.json (the manifest) is required, in the image at /a12s/service.json or inline as services.<name>.manifest:
  `{"a12s": 1, "name": "clock", "version": "1.0.0", "user": 1000, "health": {"http": {"port": 8080, "path":
  "/healthz"}}}`. `user` is a non-zero uid (match the image's USER). Optional: `ports`
  ({"api": {"port": 8080, "protocol": "http"}}, add "mcp": {"path": "/mcp"} to expose an MCP server to agent
  computers that `uses:` it), `credentials` ([{"name": "x", "required": false}]), `state` ({"at": "/var/lib/svc",
  "size": "1Gi"}), `tmpfs`, `resources`.
- The process runs as that uid, read-only root filesystem, no capabilities; write to `state.at` or a `tmpfs` path.
  Reaches the internet only through its own `egress.allow`. A Service that exits is restarted with backoff.
  Credentials it names are files at /run/a12s/secrets/<name>.
- Any language works: read config.json, call POST $A12S_API/v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox (body as in HTTP API) with
  the client certificate in /run/a12s/tls/{ca.crt,cert.pem,key.pem}.
- In Go, svckit (package `github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s/services/svckit` inside the a12s module, v0.8.1; no separate
  module or tag) does the config, mTLS client, send and health check. A complete clock (go.mod, main.go,
  service.json, Dockerfile): https://github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s-cookbook/tree/main/examples/go-service
- Build the image before `a12s up` (a12s doesn't build it); `a12s service logs <svc> -f` shows its output. No
  Service needed for a plain schedule: host cron running `a12s -F ~/proj/fleet.yaml send lead "…" --replace daily`.

## Browser (gateway)

`a12s gateway` serves your app and, on the same origin, the API at /v1/ under a scoped token the page never sees.
The page imports the npm package through a bundler (Vite, …); that is the only way in, and `Fleet.connect()` with no
arguments finds the API. Run it in the Fleet's directory (or -F path/fleet.yaml).

`a12s gateway -- npx vite` runs your dev server behind it (or `-- npm run dev`: Next.js, …; hot reload included),
`--dev http://localhost:5173` uses one already running, `--web dist` serves a built app. It prints and opens
http://127.0.0.1:7012/?key=… (new key each run; `--no-open` only prints). Open that link, not the dev server's own
port: the key becomes a cookie that /v1/ needs. No dev-server config is needed: the gateway waits for the
http://localhost:<port> URL the command prints (or `--dev-port <port>`). Scripts and tests use the key as a token:
Fleet.connect({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:7012", token: key }). The page may use status, events, send and
inbox on every agent computer, not create or change them; narrow with `--allow status,events` and
`--agent-computers worker`. Messages from the page arrive via token:gateway-7012. Loopback only; to serve other
people, run your own server with login that calls a12s with a narrow or prefix token (see CLI).
A page with a send box and live events: https://github.com/coltonkirsten/a12s-cookbook/tree/main/examples/gateway-page

## HTTP API (any language)

- Base http://127.0.0.1:<port>, header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, both from ~/.a12s/<fleet>/controller.json
  ({"port", "token"}: the owner token), or a token from `a12s token create`. Errors are {code, message, fix}.
  Every route, field, event and error code: docs/api.md.
- Send: POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox {"body", "sender"?, "metadata"?, "fresh"?, "expires"? (seconds), "replaceKey"?}
  → {id, state, …}.
- One agent computer: PUT /v1/agent-computers/{c} with its spec as JSON (fleet.yaml's fields; seccomp is the profile
  object) creates or replaces it; `If-None-Match: *` only creates (409 exists if taken). PATCH is a JSON merge patch
  (null falls back to the default). Last write wins. A write answers `agentComputer: {name, spec, effective,
  status}` and takes ?dryRun=true (lists the changes, changes nothing). The same on /v1/services/{s}.
- The whole Fleet: GET /v1/fleet → {version, fleet} with ETag "<version>"; PUT /v1/fleet {"fleet": …} with
  If-Match: "<version>" answers 412 version_mismatch if it changed since you read it.
- Events (SSE): GET /v1/events is the whole Fleet on one stream (?agentComputers=a,b filters); GET
  /v1/agent-computers/{c}/events is one journal (?turn=<id> replays one Turn, then stays open: stop at its
  turn.finished). Last-Event-ID resumes, `event: head` marks live, `event: gap` = events lost (resync: /v1/status).
- Tokens (owner only): POST /v1/tokens {"name", "prefix"} or {"name", "actions", "computers": [names] or ["*"]}
  → {…, secret} (shown once). A prefix token may do what the owner can on agent computers, Services and credentials
  whose names start with its prefix; their grants.send and uses (defaults included: override a default grant outside
  it) must stay inside it, else 403 out_of_prefix. /v1/fleet, drives, tokens, security.seccomp and attach are 403
  forbidden.
  Reads list only its names.
- Error codes an app branches on: not_found (404), exists, in_use, busy (409), no_grant, forbidden, out_of_prefix
  (403), version_mismatch (412), inbox_full (429), asleep (503).

## API surface

<!-- api-surface: generated by `go test ./internal/controller -run TestLLMsTxtSurface -update`; do not edit -->
Routes, with the action a narrow token needs (owner: the owner token only; prefix: a prefix token, for names inside it). A prefix token may also make every action route on names inside its prefix.

```text
GET /v1/fleet                                   owner
PUT /v1/fleet                                   owner
GET /v1/status                                  status
GET /v1/agent-computers                         status
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}                     status
PUT /v1/agent-computers/{c}                     owner, or prefix
PATCH /v1/agent-computers/{c}                   owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/agent-computers/{c}                  owner, or prefix
GET /v1/events                                  events
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/events              events
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/turns               events
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/turns/{id}/stop    stop
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/stop               stop
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/power              power
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/shell              owner, or prefix
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/terminal            owner, or prefix
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/terminal/{id}/resize owner, or prefix
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/files               owner, or prefix
PUT /v1/agent-computers/{c}/files               owner, or prefix
GET /v1/drives                                  owner
DELETE /v1/drives/{d}                           owner
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox              send
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox               inbox
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}          send or inbox
GET /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}/events   send or inbox
DELETE /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/{id}       send or inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/clear        inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/hold         inbox
POST /v1/agent-computers/{c}/inbox/resume       inbox
GET /v1/services                                status
GET /v1/services/{s}                            status
PUT /v1/services/{s}                            owner, or prefix
PATCH /v1/services/{s}                          owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/services/{s}                         owner, or prefix
GET /v1/services/{s}/logs                       owner, or prefix
POST /v1/services/{s}/power                     owner, or prefix
POST /v1/services/{s}/shell                     owner, or prefix
GET /v1/credentials                             owner, or prefix
PUT /v1/credentials/{name}                      owner, or prefix
DELETE /v1/credentials/{name}                   owner, or prefix
POST /v1/tokens                                 owner
GET /v1/tokens                                  owner
DELETE /v1/tokens/{name}                        owner
```

SDK objects (Python names; TypeScript is camelCase):

- Fleet: TypeScript get, replace, events, turns, status; Python close, status, events, turns, get, replace; Python AsyncFleet aclose, status, events, turns, get, replace
- AgentComputers: TypeScript create, get, list; Python create, get, list
- AgentComputer: TypeScript reload, update, remove, send, events, turns, sleep, wake, hold, resume, stop, inbox, message, withdraw; Python reload, send, events, turns, update, sleep, wake, hold, resume, stop, inbox, message, withdraw, remove
- Services: TypeScript create, get, list; Python create, get, list
- Service: TypeScript reload, update, remove, sleep, wake; Python reload, update, sleep, wake, remove
- Tokens: TypeScript create, list, remove; Python create, list, remove
- Credentials: TypeScript set, list, remove; Python set, list, remove
<!-- /api-surface -->

## Patterns and gotchas

- For the Turn that delivers your own Message, use `send(...).wait()`: it can't miss it, however late you call it.
  To follow Turns your Message causes on OTHER agent computers (lead's final answer in the hand-off recipe comes in
  a later Turn), open `fleet.turns()` first (`await turns.ready()` / `with fleet.turns(...)`), then send.
- Test wakeOnMessage by sleeping it (plain `sleep()`, not hold) and sending from a listed sender. After a send,
  reload() and check `status.phase` until it is Busy or Ready; an old Ready event proves nothing.
- A seccomp profile's archMap/architectures take libseccomp names only (SCMP_ARCH_X86_64, SCMP_ARCH_X86,
  SCMP_ARCH_X32, SCMP_ARCH_AARCH64, SCMP_ARCH_ARM, …); the simplest valid profile that runs everything is
  `{"defaultAction": "SCMP_ACT_ALLOW"}` (a12s warns that it allows every syscall).
- Agent computers made from code are for work that comes and goes (one per task, user or branch): create,
  send(...).wait(), remove. Keep long-lived roles in fleet.yaml; `a12s up` removes what the file doesn't list.
- Send each new task with fresh=true so the agent starts a new conversation; without it, the agent remembers
  earlier tasks and may repeat an old answer.
- An agent can only `send` to agent computers in its grants.send; anything else gets 403 no_grant. A grant may name
  an agent computer that doesn't exist yet (the write warns), so a pair can be created from code one after the other.
- Every Claude Code Turn logs one or two `egress.denied` events for telemetry hosts: harmless.
- Background work survives Turns, not the session: stop, sleep (manual or sleepAfterIdle), restart_harness, a
  fresh=true Message and a config change end it (task.finished status killed or stopped). sleepAfterIdle and staged
  config changes wait while it runs, so a never-ending one (a dev server) keeps the agent computer awake until
  `a12s stop <c>`.
- Nothing is delivered? `a12s inbox <c>` (held? says why; `a12s inbox resume <c>`), `a12s status` (asleep?
  `a12s wake <c>`), `a12s doctor`.
- attach: Docker Desktop must share the folder (/Users, /Volumes, /private, /tmp, /var/folders by default; else
  Settings > Resources > File sharing); a folder Docker can't see puts the agent computer in Error with that fix.
  Mac bind mounts are slower than drives: keep node_modules, .venv and build output in `keep` (also keeps Linux
  binaries out of your macOS folder; an empty directory marks each in your folder). The harness starts in
  /home/agent: tell it in instructions to work in ~/<name>. Ownership: on Docker Desktop files stay yours; on Linux
  the agent writes as uid 1000, so the folder must be writable by it. Nothing merges: when you and the agent edit
  the same file, the last save wins. The agent can delete anything in a writable folder: commit first.
- Upgrading a12s: install the new release, rebuild custom images FROM the new slim under new tags, `a12s up`.
  After Docker or the Controller restarts, the Controller resumes the Fleet with the credentials it stored.
- On the GCE driver (an operator's choice in ~/.a12s/<fleet>/driver.yaml, not a Fleet field) each
  agent computer is its own VM: wakes take tens of seconds, no Services, no attach, no `a12s shell` (the API's terminal and files routes work). With per-computer
  identity, status's `agentComputers[].identity` is the service account to grant access to. An app in the VPC
  reaches the API at https://<controller address>:7000 when driver.yaml sets `api: { listen: internal }`; it must
  trust the fleet's CA (docs/drivers/gce.md#reaching-the-api-from-the-vpc).
